fact_en: Giant clams in Philippine coral reefs use special light-reflecting cells called iridocytes to scatter sunlight and protect their internal algae!
fact_bis: Ang mga dako nga clam sa coral reef sa Pilipinas mogamit og special light-reflecting cells nga iridocytes aron i-scatter ang adlaw ug protektahan ang algae!

findings.note: title_bis "Iridocytes sa Tahong" names TAHONG = green mussel, a different animal from the giant clam (taklobo) the card is about. The card's own body keeps the correct thing ("Ang mga dako nga clam sa coral reef") and the terms are literally "giant clams" — so the title is the outlier. A child reading the title learns that mussels have iridocytes and host algae, which is false.

fact_en: Heat always travels from a warmer object to a cooler one! That is why a metal spoon gets hot in boiling soup.
fact_bis: Kanunay nga moadto ang kainit gikan sa mas init nga butang paingon sa mas bugnaw! Mao nga ang metal nga kutsara mokusog sa nagbukal nga sabaw.

findings.note: "ang metal nga kutsara MOKUSOG sa nagbukal nga sabaw" = the spoon becomes strong/intense, not hot (moinit). The card's concrete claim — the metal spoon GETS HOT in boiling soup — is never stated in Cebuano; a child has to infer it from the general warm->cool sentence before it.

fact_en:
How does your brain tell your leg to kick a soccer ball?

Your brain sends rapid electrical impulses through your nerves to tell your leg muscles to kick!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsulti sa imong utok sa imong tiil aron i-kick ang soccer ball?

Nagpadala ang imong utok ug paspas nga electrical impulses sa mga nerves aron sultihan ang mga kalamnan sa tiil!

findings.note: title_bis "Utak Binti Bulan Sulti" drops BULAN = MOON into a card about the brain telling the leg to kick a soccer ball. Nothing in the en/bis body or terms mentions the moon (body is correct: utok -> electrical impulses -> kalamnan sa tiil). Looks like a corruption of "bola"; as shipped the title names a thing that is not in the card.

fact_en: A short circuit bypasses the normal electrical path, making electrons flow unrestricted and generate dangerous, melting heat in the wires!
fact_bis: Ang short circuit mopasulod sa normal nga electrical path, hinungdan nga ang electrons molabay nga walay limitasyon ug maghimo og delikado nga kainit nga makatunaw sa wires!

findings.note: "Ang short circuit MOPASULOD sa normal nga electrical path" says the short circuit ENTERS / feeds into the normal electrical path — the reverse of the English "bypasses the normal electrical path" (should be molaktaw / molikay). The definitional fact of the card (a short circuit skips the normal path) is inverted and never corrected anywhere on the card; only the consequence (unrestricted flow, melting heat) survives.

fact_en:
Can a magnet really make a frog float?

Yes! The world's strongest continuous magnetic fields from lab electromagnets reach 45 Tesla, strong enough to levitate a live frog!
fact_bis:
Makapahuyop ba gyud ang magnet sa buhi nga baki?

Oo! Ang pinakakusog nga continuous magnetic field gikan sa lab electromagnets nakaabot og 45 Tesla, nga makapahuyop sa buhi nga baki!

findings.note: Body uses "makapahuyop" twice for levitate/float — HUYOP = to blow (with breath), not to float (palutaw). Both the question and the answer become "can a magnet make a live frog blow?", so the body never states the card's only fact (a 45-Tesla field can levitate a live frog). Recoverable ONLY from the one-word keyword title ("...Palaka Lutaw"); drop this flag if title-restoration counts as recovery.

fact_en: During the reflection stage of vision, light rays bounce off a non-luminous object like a book and travel right into your eyes!
fact_bis: Sa reflection stage sa vision, mopakpak ang light rays gikan sa dili nag-sidlak nga butang sama sa libro ug mo-adto sa imong mga mata!

findings.note: title_bis "Pamalandong sa Hayag" for "Light Reflection": pamalandong is contemplation/meditation, the mental sense of "reflection", not light bouncing (salamin/pagbanaag). The card's own body keeps the optical sense ("Sa reflection stage sa vision, mopakpak ang light rays..."), and sibling cards in this batch use physical phrasing (ffct-28394 "Salamin sa Flip", ffct-28523 "Nabalik nga Kahayag"), so the title is the outlier. A child reading the title alone is told the card is about pondering, not about light.

fact_en: Fiberglass insulation traps air to slow down heat transfer, keeping your house cozy and warm during winter!
fact_bis: Ang fiberglass insulation nag-trapo sa hangin aron mapugngan ang pag-balhin sa kainit, mao nga mapainit gihapon ang balay sa tingtugnaw!

findings.note: "Ang fiberglass insulation nag-trapo sa hangin" for "traps air": trapo is a rag / to wipe, so the Cebuano says the insulation WIPES the air. The trapped-air mechanism is the card's only explanation of why heat transfer slows, and nothing else in the card restores it. Compare ffct-28426 in the same batch, which writes the verb correctly as "pag-trap".

fact_en:
Ever wonder how you jump so high in luksong-tinik?

Your strong leg muscles push your body upward! But don't worry, gravity will always pull you safely back down to the ground.
fact_bis:
Nganong maka-tulon ka ug taas sa luksong-tinik?

Ang kusgang unod sa imong mga bitiis motulod sa imong lawas paibabaw! Apan ang gravity mobira kanimo balik sa yuta.

findings.note: Body question reads "Nganong maka-tulon ka ug taas sa luksong-tinik?" — tulon in Cebuano is TO SWALLOW; jump is lukso (Tagalog-interference from talon). The card's own title_bis ("Paglukso ug Grabidad") uses lukso correctly, which is the strongest evidence the body verb is the defect. The card's question sentence asks why you can swallow high.

fact_en: The solid, opaque brick walls of Vigan's heritage houses block light energy, keeping the indoor rooms dark and cool!
fact_bis: Ang solid, opaque nga brick walls sa Vigan heritage houses nagbabag sa light energy, mao nga ang sulod magpabiling ngitngit ug bugnaw!

findings.note: title_bis "Vigan Luto Malamig" for "Vigan Cool Brick Walls": malamig is Tagalog (Cebuano is bugnaw, which the card's own body uses), and luto in Cebuano means COOKED, not brick (tisa/ladrilyo). The title reads roughly "Vigan Cooked Cold" and names neither walls nor bricks; only the body carries the fact.

fact_en: Your heart uses tiny electrical impulses from the sinoatrial node to trigger muscle contractions and pump blood throughout your body!
fact_bis: Ang imong kasingkasing naggamit og gagmay nga electrical impulses gikan sa sinoatrial node aron ma-trigger ang muscle contractions ug mag-pump og dugo sa tibuok lawas!

findings.note: title_bis "SA Node Kasing" — kasing on its own is a SPINNING TOP in Cebuano; the heart is kasingkasing. The body uses kasingkasing correctly twice, so the truncated title names a different object. This is a title-only wrong word, not compact-title style, because the shortened form is itself a real and different Cebuano noun.

fact_en: After gliding above the ocean waves, gravity pulls the flying fish back down into the water to safety!
fact_bis: Human makalupad sa ibabaw sa ocean waves, gihurot sa gravity ang flying fish pabalik sa tubig aron luwas!

findings.note: "gihurot sa gravity ang flying fish pabalik sa tubig" for "gravity pulls the flying fish back down": hurot means to use up / finish off / wipe out, not to pull (bira/butong). The card's single claim is what gravity DOES to the fish, and the verb names consumption rather than a downward pull; nothing elsewhere in the card supplies the correct verb.

fact_en: Your vocal cords vibrate to produce sound waves, which then travel through the air for others to hear!
fact_bis: Ang imong vocal cords mobati ug maghimo og sound waves, nga molakaw sa hangin aron madungog sa uban!

findings.note: Medium confidence. EN: "Your vocal cords VIBRATE to produce sound waves"; BIS: "Ang imong vocal cords MOBATI ug maghimo og sound waves". `bati` means to feel/greet (or bad/ugly) in Cebuano, never to vibrate (`mokurog`/`mo-uyog`). The vibration mechanism is unrecoverable from this card; its two near-duplicates ffct-28570 and ffct-28638 both use `mo-vibrate` correctly, so this card is the outlier. Flagged as lower severity because the rest of the sentence (sound waves travel through air to be heard) still lands.
